questions: Do your hands tremble when they are resting in your lap?
Did you notice the stiffness or slowness start on one side of your body?
Do you feel dizzy or lightheaded when you stand up quickly?
Do you have difficulty controlling your bladder?
Are you taking any medications for nausea, stomach problems, or mental health conditions?
Do you have trouble moving your eyes when looking up or down?
Do you have a family member with a similar movement problem?
Do you have excessive drooling or difficulty swallowing?
Have you ever had a sudden brief episode where you lost awareness or "zoned out"?
Did your walking problem start suddenly after an emotional event or stressful situation?
Do you find that your symptoms get worse when you are being watched or examined?
Are your symptoms inconsistent - sometimes better, sometimes worse for no clear reason?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your feet or hands?
Have you had any problems with balance that worsen when you close your eyes or in the dark?
Have you been diagnosed with thyroid problems or diabetes?
orders: Detailed gait analysis with timed walking, stride length measurement, and assessment for magnetic gait
Bedside assessment of cognition using Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA)
CT head without contrast (to look for ventriculomegaly disproportionate to atrophy)
Detailed cerebellar examination: finger-to-nose testing, heel-to-shin testing, rapid alternating movements
Vibration sense testing at the ankles
Brain MRI with thin cuts through the posterior fossa to assess cerebellar volume and look for structural lesions
Onset assessment: when exactly did you first notice the unsteadiness and was it gradual or sudden?
Brain MRI of the posterior fossa with thin cuts through the cerebellum and brainstem
